questions.explanation: C4 to A4 is a major sixth, nine semitones. A minor sixth would be eight semitones.
questions.hint: Major sixth is nine half steps.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The interval pattern of a major scale
questions.learningObjective: Build a major scale on F
questions.stem: A graph builds a major scale on F using W W H W W W H; which note is the fourth degree?

options.text: B natural is the fourth degree of F major.
B flat is the fourth degree of F major.
A is the fourth degree of F major.
C is the fourth degree of F major.

questions.explanation: From F, whole to G, whole to A, half to B flat gives B flat as the fourth degree. The distractors misplace steps or ignore the flat.
questions.hint: Apply the half step after A.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Whole step and half step in equal temperament
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish equal temperament half steps
questions.stem: A graph compares two adjacent keys; what defines a half step in equal temperament?

options.text: A half step is any interval between white keys.
A half step equals two whole steps.
A half step is the smallest interval in the system.
A half step is the same as an octave.

questions.explanation: In equal temperament the half step is the smallest interval. The distractors reverse, color-code, or magnify it.
questions.hint: Half step is the basic unit.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Naming an interval by number and quality
questions.learningObjective: Name a compound interval
questions.stem: How do you name an interval larger than an octave?

answer.exemplar: Name it as a compound interval by adding seven to the simple interval number, such as a tenth for a third plus an octave.

questions.explanation: Compound intervals add seven to the simple interval number. This keeps the quality while reflecting the larger span.
questions.hint: Add seven to the simple number.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Perfect, major, minor, augmented and diminished
questions.learningObjective: Diminish an interval
questions.stem: A perfect fifth has seven semitones; how many semitones in a diminished fifth?
questions.explanation: Diminishing lowers the interval by one semitone, so six remain. Six also defines an augmented fourth.
questions.hint: Lower by one semitone.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Semitone count for a named interval
questions.learningObjective: Count semitones in a major third
questions.stem: A graph shows C to E; how many semitones separate them?

options.text: Two semitones separate C from E.
Three semitones separate C from E.
Five semitones separate C from E.
Four semitones separate C from E.

questions.explanation: C to E is a major third, four semitones. The distractors supply counts for nearby intervals.
questions.hint: Major third is four half steps.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: What an inversion does to quality and number
questions.learningObjective: Invert a major sixth
questions.stem: A graph inverts a major sixth; what interval results?

options.text: A major third results from inverting a major sixth.
A minor third results from inverting a major sixth.
A minor sixth results from inverting a major sixth.
A perfect fourth results from inverting a major sixth.

questions.explanation: Nine minus six is three, and major becomes minor, giving a minor third. The distractors fail one part of the rule.
questions.hint: Nine minus six is three.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: What a key signature holds
questions.learningObjective: Read a flat key signature
questions.stem: A score shows three flats at the staff start; which notes are affected?

answer.exemplar: B, E, and A are lowered by a semitone throughout the piece unless an accidental cancels one.

questions.explanation: Three flats lower B, E, and A. The performer applies them unless cancelled by an accidental.
questions.hint: Three flats: B, E, A.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Relative major and relative minor
questions.learningObjective: Build a relative minor triad
questions.stem: C major and A minor are relative; how many semitones separate C from A?
questions.explanation: C down to A is a minor third, nine semitones downward. The relative minor tonic sits a minor third below.
questions.hint: Down a minor third.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Why the circle of fifths is ordered as it is
questions.learningObjective: Explain flat side of circle
questions.stem: A graph moves counterclockwise on the circle of fifths; what happens to the key signature?

options.text: Each step removes all accidentals.
Each step adds one sharp by moving up a fifth.
Each step adds one flat by moving down a fifth.
Each step changes the meter instead.

questions.explanation: Counterclockwise moves down a fifth and adds one flat. The distractors reverse direction or change the wrong element.
questions.hint: Counterclockwise adds flats.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The leading tone and its pull
questions.learningObjective: Identify the leading tone in minor
questions.stem: A graph raises the seventh degree in a minor scale; what is that raised degree called?

options.text: It is the dominant, a fifth above the tonic.
It is the subtonic, a whole step below the tonic.
It is the mediant, a third above the tonic.
It is the leading tone, a semitone below the tonic.

questions.explanation: Raising the seventh degree creates a leading tone a semitone below the tonic. Without raising it remains a subtonic.
questions.hint: Raised seventh becomes leading tone.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Subdominant and dominant function
questions.learningObjective: Name the dominant chord
questions.stem: On which scale degree is the dominant chord built and what is its Roman numeral?

answer.exemplar: The dominant chord is built on the fifth scale degree and receives Roman numeral V in major and minor keys.

questions.explanation: The fifth degree carries dominant function and receives numeral V. The subdominant would be IV instead.
questions.hint: Dominant is degree five, numeral V.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Chords built in thirds and the numeral that names them
questions.learningObjective: Name the mediant triad
questions.stem: A triad built on the third scale degree is the mediant; what is its Roman numeral?
questions.explanation: The numeral matches the scale degree, so degree three receives III. The value is the degree number.
questions.hint: Numeral equals degree number.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Octave equivalence
questions.learningObjective: Test octave equivalence with intervals
questions.stem: A graph transposes every note up one octave; which property of the melody is unchanged?

options.text: The absolute frequencies of all notes are unchanged.
The interval pattern between successive notes is unchanged.
The octave numbers of all notes are unchanged.
The key signature changes by one sharp.

questions.explanation: Transposing by an octave preserves interval patterns and pitch classes. Frequencies and octave numbers change.
questions.hint: Intervals stay the same.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Scientific pitch notation and middle C
questions.learningObjective: Compare two labeled notes
questions.stem: A graph labels a note as C3 and another as C4; which is higher?

options.text: They are the same pitch because letters match.
C3 is one octave higher than C4.
C4 is one octave higher than C3.
Neither has a defined height.

questions.explanation: A larger octave number means a higher register, so C4 is above C3. The distractors reverse or ignore that.
questions.hint: Higher number means higher pitch.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The interval pattern of a major scale
questions.learningObjective: Compare major scale to natural minor
questions.stem: How does the natural minor scale pattern differ from the major scale pattern?

answer.exemplar: Natural minor uses whole, half, whole, whole, half, whole, whole, moving the half steps to different scale-degree boundaries.

questions.explanation: Natural minor shifts the half steps to degrees two-three and five-six. The major pattern places them at three-four and seven-eight.
questions.hint: Half steps move to two-three and five-six.

questions.topic: Whole step and half step in equal temperament
questions.learningObjective: Count semitones in a chromatic step
questions.stem: How many semitones are in one chromatic half step?
questions.explanation: A chromatic half step is one semitone. Two semitones would make a whole step.
questions.hint: One half step is one semitone.
